sessionName: Week 21 - Keeping and growing PE relationships revisited
summary: Luke Badiali revisited retention and expansion with Thomas Avery and Grace Lindqvist, 12 weeks after the week 9 session. The 100-day market sprint sold only once at 60k, while three sponsors asked for help preparing portfolio companies for exit. We changed two positions: key account coverage now focuses on 5 PE houses with a named director pairing, and the post-deal offer is now an exit readiness review rather than the 100-day sprint.

discussion.keyPoints: Grace reported one 100-day sprint sold in 12 weeks. Sponsors said their operating partners already cover the 100-day plan. Three sponsors instead asked about vendor due diligence preparation 12 to 18 months before exit.
Thomas said spreading attention across 8 key accounts was too thin. Three of the eight are now largely using their own in-house teams. Luke proposed concentrating on the 5 most active PE houses.
The 20-minute debrief calls are working and have been held on 9 of 11 reports. One of the two quiet accounts came back after its free sector briefing.

recommendations.recommendation: Focus key account coverage on 5 PE houses, each with a partner and a director pairing and a monthly touchpoint. This replaces the earlier approach of naming all 8 top PE houses with a quarterly relationship review.
Offer an exit readiness review at 75k to sponsors 12 to 18 months before a planned exit. This replaces the earlier 100-day value creation market sprint at 60k, which is withdrawn.
Keep the 20-minute debrief call within two weeks of every report.
Run the free sector briefing win-back with the remaining quiet account.
Ask satisfied deal partners for introductions to their portfolio company CEOs.

actions.action: Agree partner and director pairings for the 5 key accounts
Write the exit readiness review scope and a one-page offer

nextFocus: Test the exit readiness review with the three sponsors who asked about it.
nextPreparation: Grace to bring a draft exit readiness scope and the list of portfolio companies expected to exit in 2027 and 2028.
